newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures end lower, locked in range.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures end lower, locked in range.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended lower Thursday, with light arbitrage sales the only standout of a quiet trading day, dealers said.

Prices dipped below unchanged from the outset, weighed down by scattered speculative selling. The market drifted in negative territory for the rest of the session, as currency-linked selling against London cocoa pushed New York to the day's lows.

Traders said March's failure the previous day to fill a recent chart gap at $1,375-1,378 sent a bearish signal, contributing to today's weakness. But scale-down industry buying once again provided support at the lows.
March cocoa finished down $10 per tonne, to $1,364, having traded from $1,363 to $1,374. May eased $11 to $1,386, while the outer months fell $9 to $14.
Overall volume was sparse, at an estimated 4,196 lots on the day.
